To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) for a K-user linear channel with symmetric cross-correlations and AWGN noise the list detection algorithm finds the P sequences of highest a posteriori probabilities in time O(K/sup K/+PlogP) and 2) for any multiuser detection problem with an optimal detection algorithm that is of polynomial complexity, the list detection algorithm is of polynomial complexity.

(i) a list detection algorithm for the K-symmetrical multiple-access channel is proposed; (ii) the list detection algorithm can be incorporated into iterative decoding schemes; and (iii) the list detection approach can be applied to other multiuser systems with polynomial complexity optimal detection algorithms.
the problem of finding the K most probable binary sequences of length N over a K-symmetrical channel with additive white gaussian noise can be solved with complexity O(K/sup K/+K/sup 2/ logK).
In summary, our research is concerned with
a general approach for the efficient computation of marginal probabilities for the multiple-access channel.
the development of efficient algorithms for the detection and decoding of multiuser systems.
the problem of finding the P most probable codewords for a K-symmetric multiple access channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is an excellent alternative to the conventional approach for multiple-user detection.
the proposed algorithm is a very promising candidate for iterative decoding of linear multiple-access channels.
the proposed algorithm is the first to provide a computationally efficient list detector for multiple-access channels with additive white Gaussian interference.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the K-symmetric channel has a simple, low-complexity, list-detection algorithm that can be used to obtain very good performance in an iterative multiple-user decoder.
we provide a new approach to iterative multiple-access decoding, which has a polynomial complexity and is applicable to a wide range of channels.
the proposed algorithm can be used as an alternative to the iterative decoding algorithm for the K-symmetrical channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to achieve very good performance in the case of iterative multiple-user detection by using a very small list size.
for many practical systems, it is possible to approximate the APP by a small number of most probable sequences.
it is possible to find good approximations to marginalization over all possible sequences with polynomial complexity in the number of users.
